questions.title: Ball hits a marker on the green
questions.question: You putt your ball on the green. It accidentally hits another player's small round marker and stops in a new place. What should you do?

choices.text: Play your ball from where it stops, with no penalty.
Pick up your ball and put it, and the marker, back to where they were.
Move your ball back to where it started and keep playing.
Add one extra shot and putt again from the start.

questions.explanation: If your ball bumps into a marker on the green, just play your ball from its new spot. You do not get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A small, flat object that marks where someone’s ball was on the green.
The short, smooth grass around the hole.

questions.teachingTip: Show children ball-markers and let them practise marking a ball on the green. Ask them to pretend to putt and help them understand what happens if a ball hits a marker.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think you always have to move the ball back to where it started.
They may worry about getting a penalty if their ball hits a marker.

questions.title: Ball hits a ball-marker
questions.question: If your ball accidentally hits a ball-marker on the green and is deflected to a new spot, what should you do?

choices.text: Play the ball from where it comes to rest with no penalty.
Replace your ball and the marker.
Move the ball back to its original spot and continue.
Add one penalty stroke and replay the putt.

questions.explanation: If your ball strikes a ball-marker on the green, you play the ball from where it ends up, with no penalty.
